hook: The Moon is about as far from the Sun as Earth, yet its surface swings from about 120 °C in sunlight to below −170 °C at night. Earth’s average stays near 15 °C. The difference is a blanket of gases a few kilometers thick that lets sunlight in but slows heat on its way out.

prereq.q: What does the stratospheric ozone layer absorb?
options: Heat given off by the ground
prereq.why: The ozone layer absorbs incoming UV; it is a different process from the one in this topic.

prereq.q: Which gas is released when fossil fuels are burned?
prereq.why: Burning fossil fuels combines their carbon with oxygen, releasing CO₂.

figure.caption: The greenhouse effect (left) and the ozone layer (right): different gases, different radiation, different layers.

chain.cause: Sunlight, mostly visible light, passes through the air
The warm surface gives off infrared radiation
chain.effect: greenhouse gases in the troposphere absorb much of it

chain.cause: The gases re-emit that energy in all directions, part of it back down
chain.effect: the lower atmosphere and surface stay warmer than they would be
traps more heat, strengthening the effect and raising temperatures

ideas: The greenhouse effect: greenhouse gases absorb infrared radiation given off by the surface and re-emit part of it downward, warming the lower atmosphere.
Greenhouse gases: water vapor (most abundant), carbon dioxide, methane, nitrous oxide (N₂O) and CFCs and HFCs. SO₂ and particulates are not greenhouse gases.
Global warming potential (GWP) compares the heat trapped by a gas with the same mass of CO₂ over 100 years: CO₂ 1, methane about 28, N₂O about 265, CFCs thousands.
The natural greenhouse effect keeps Earth about 33 °C warmer than it would be. Ozone depletion is a separate problem: UV and the stratosphere.

misconception.wrong: The ozone hole lets heat in, and that is the cause of global warming.
misconception.right: The ozone hole lets in more UV, which raises skin cancer. Warming comes from greenhouse gases trapping outgoing infrared in the lower atmosphere. CFCs are the one link: they do both.

summary: Sunlight warms the surface, which gives off infrared; greenhouse gases (water vapor, CO₂, methane, nitrous oxide, CFCs) absorb it and send part back down, keeping Earth about 33 °C warmer. More gas traps more heat. Global warming potential compares gases with CO₂: multiply a mass by its GWP for CO₂ equivalent. The greenhouse effect is not ozone depletion.
